chunks: Ismāʿīl ibn Muḥammad ibn ʿAlī ibn Ismāʿīl ibn ʿAlī ibn ʿAbd Allāh ibn ʿAbbās ibn ʿAbd al-Muṭṭalib narrated to me, saying:

I sat in wait for Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام) on the roadside. When he passed by me, I complained to him of my need, and I swore to him that I did not have a single dirham or anything above it, nor any lunch nor dinner.

He said: He (عليه السلام) said, "You are swearing by Allah falsely, while you have buried two hundred dinars. What I say is not to withhold the gift from you. O servant, give him what you have." So his servant gave me one hundred dinars. Then he turned to me and said, "You will be deprived of them at the time when you are most in need of them," meaning the dinars that I had buried.

And he (عليه السلام) spoke the truth, and it happened just as he said. I had buried two hundred dinars and said, "It will be support and refuge for us." Then I was struck by intense necessity for something to spend, and the doors of livelihood were closed to me. So I dug for it, only to find that a son of mine had come to know its location, taken it, and fled, and I could not recover anything of it.

key_terms.أَبْوَابُ الرِّزْقِ: the means and openings of livelihood
key_terms.الْحَاجَةَ: need or hardship that prompted the complaint
key_terms.تُحْرَمُهَا: you will be deprived of it
key_terms.دِينَارٍ: gold coin; a unit of wealth

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith show the truthfulness and divine knowledge of Imam Abū Muḥammad (عليه السلام)?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates an encounter with Imam Abū Muḥammad al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī (عليه السلام), in which he reveals hidden knowledge about a man's buried wealth and still grants him financial assistance. It also recounts the fulfillment of the Imam's warning that the man would be deprived of that buried money at the time of greatest need, highlighting both the Imam's truthfulness and the moral gravity of false oaths.
